voices.note: the Gemara's own voice of this piska: its questions (מאי, מיבעי ליה, למה לי, אטו, ותו ליכא, מנלן), its unattributed answers and derashot on new lemmas, the narrative of 12b.7-8, 13a.22-23, 16a.4-11, 16a.14, 16a.17, its kashya/teyuvta at 14a.9 and 15a.4
Rebbi (12b.14-15), and 'רבינו' of the tanna at 14a.12
תנו רבנן (14a.4): forty-eight prophets and seven prophetesses
כדתניא (14a.7, recalled at 14a.9): song outside the Land

props.gloss_en: the Rabbis taught: forty-eight prophets and seven prophetesses prophesied to Israel and neither subtracted from nor added to what is written in the Torah, except for the reading of the Megilla
what did they expound? R' Chiya bar Avin in R' Yehoshua ben Korcha's name: if from slavery to freedom we say song, from death to life all the more so
[the stam answers:] because Hallel is not said over a miracle outside the Land
a baraita: until Israel entered the Land all lands were fit for saying song [over their miracles]; once Israel entered the Land, the other lands were no longer fit
Rav Nachman: its reading [of the Megilla] is its Hallel
Rava: granted there [Egypt], 'praise, servants of the Lord' -- and not servants of Pharaoh; but here, 'and not servants of Ahasuerus'? we are still servants of Ahasuerus
once they were exiled, [the lands] returned to their original fitness
but it is written 'there was a man from Ramatayim-Tzofim' (1 Sam 1:1) -- one of two hundred seers who prophesied to Israel
there were indeed many, but prophecy needed for the generations was written and that not needed was not written
a baraita: many prophets arose for Israel, double the number of those who left Egypt
R' Shmuel bar Nachmani: a man who came from two heights that face each other
R' Chanin: a man descended from people who stand at the height of the world
and who are they? the sons of Korach, as written 'and the sons of Korach did not die' (Num 26:11)
a tanna in the name of our master [Rebbi]: a place was set apart for them in Gehinnom and they stood upon it
